control: wrong formula (CED 1.3.A.2 gives x = x_0 + v_x0 t + (1/2) a_x t^2; the factor of one half is dropped here)
title: Position with constant acceleration
body: x = x_0 + v_{x0} t + a_x t^2

control: explicitly excluded by the CED (1.3 BOUNDARY STATEMENT: AP Physics 1 does not expect students to quantitatively analyze nonuniform acceleration)
title: Jerk: the rate of change of acceleration
body: j = \frac{\Delta a}{\Delta t}, \text{ used to analyze motion with nonuniform acceleration quantitatively}

control: wrong owner topic (resolving vectors into perpendicular components is topic 1.5, EK 1.5.A.1-3; 1.1 covers only scalars, vectors and one-dimensional vector sums)
title: Resolving a vector into perpendicular components
body: A vector can be modeled as the resultant of two perpendicular components, resolved using trigonometric functions in a chosen coordinate system.

control: swapped graph relationships (CED 1.3.A.4.iii: displacement is the area under a velocity-time graph; 1.3.A.4.i: instantaneous velocity is the slope of a tangent to a position-time graph)
title: Reading kinematic graphs
body: What the slope and the area give on each motion graph.

items.label: Position-time graph
items.meaning: the area under the curve gives the instantaneous velocity

items.label: Velocity-time graph
items.meaning: the slope of a tangent gives the displacement

items.label: Acceleration-time graph
items.meaning: the area under the curve gives the change in velocity

control: hook expansion contradicts the CED (1.1.A.3: distance and speed are scalars while displacement and velocity are vectors). The entry is correct, so only the hook should be rejected.
title: Scalar and vector kinematic quantities
body: Scalars are described by magnitude only; vectors by both magnitude and direction.

hooks.hook_text: Speed has direction, velocity does not
hooks.when_to_use: when sorting kinematic quantities into scalars and vectors
hooks.caution: Use the CED's scalar and vector terms when answering.
